ai.title: Add Troubleshooting Install to Docs
ai.summary: Added Troubleshooting section to `web/src/content/help/getting-started.mdx`. Documents `sudo npm install -g codebuff` for Mac/Linux and admin prompt for Windows on permission errors. Recommends reinstalling Node if failure persists.

eli5.text: The help guide now includes a new section that steps users through fixing permission errors during installation. If you tried installing the tool and your computer refused the command, the guide now shows what to run on Mac or Linux (sudo npm install -g codebuff) and how to open a command prompt as an administrator on Windows. If the installer still fails, the guide points you to reinstall your JavaScript runtime. The updated instructions are live today.

ai.title: Force assistant endturn after 20 consecutive messages
ai.summary: Added a hard limit of 20 consecutive assistant messages in `mainPrompt` to force `end_turn` and return a warning string, preventing infinite loops. Introduced `lastUserPromptIndex` to `AgentState` to track the last user prompt position for accurate message counting. This change applies to the backend agent loop and shared state types.

eli5.text: The assistant will now stop and hand you back control if it sends 20 messages in a row without waiting for you to reply, rather than potentially looping forever. If you ever see it just keep talking to itself, this change is what will eventually cut it off and show you a warning that things went sideways. This safety net is now live for everyone using the core chat backend today.

ai.title: Mock logger in main-prompt tests
ai.summary: Added mocks for `logger.debug`, `logger.error`, `logger.info`, and `logger.warn` in `backend/src/__tests__/main-prompt.test.ts`. Suppresses log output during `mainPrompt` test execution. Internal change affecting test suite only.

eli5.text: During internal testing of the main assistant prompt, the system was configured to silently capture log messages that normally appear in the background. This keeps the test output clean and focused on actual test results instead of noisy informational messages. No user-facing behavior changes; this affects only the internal test suite.

ai.title: Fix filepath check in getFileReadingUpdates
ai.summary: Corrects partition logic in `getFileReadingUpdates` to check `loadedFiles[path] !== null` instead of verifying `loadedFiles.content`. Previous condition incorrectly validated a non-existent `content` property on the `loadedFiles` object rather than the file-specific entry. Scope limited to `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. Ensures accurate detection of existing vs. non-existing file paths.

eli5.text: The assistant now correctly tells whether it has already loaded a file when you ask it to read something. Previously, it checked the wrong entry in its list of loaded files, so it could think a file was loaded when it wasn't, or vice versa. You would notice this mainly in how smoothly the assistant responds when you ask it to read files repeatedly, since it now keeps a more accurate mental note of what it has already seen.

ai.title: Upgrade ignore to 7.0.3 and remove slash prefix stripping
ai.summary: Upgraded the ignore package from 5.3.2 to 7.0.3 in npm-app/package.json. Removed manual stripping of leading slashes from gitignore, codebuffignore, and manicodeignore lines in common/src/project-file-tree.ts, as v7 handles absolute path patterns natively.

eli5.text: The assistant no longer needs to manually clean up file paths before deciding which files to ignore, because the updated underlying tool now interprets those paths on its own. This means ignore rules for files like gitignore, codebuffignore, and manicodeignore are applied more accurately, matching how developers naturally write them. The change is live today and affects anyone working with project ignore files in the tool. If you looked at your ignored files while using the assistant, you'd see more of them behaving the way you'd expect based on their written rules.

ai.title: readfiles reports specific status for missing, ignored, or oversized
ai.summary: The `read_files` tool now returns explicit status strings like `[FILE_DOES_NOT_EXIST]` or `[FILE_IGNORED_BY_GITIGNORE_OR_CODEBUFF_IGNORE]` instead of generic nulls. This provides the LLM with precise context on why a file couldn't be read, improving agent reasoning. Changes span `npm-app/src/project-files.ts` for detection and `common/src/constants.ts` for status definitions. `FILE_TOO_LARGE` now includes the actual file size in MB.

eli5.text: When the assistant tries to read a file but can't, it now gets a clear reason back instead of a generic 'not found' message. You wouldn't see this directly in the app, but it helps the assistant understand why a file is missing or hidden, so it can explain things more accurately when something goes wrong. The change is live today.
